comparison.position: The local component executes only Equations5–13 reward, advantage and clipping arithmetic. QT is an explicit tuple list, not a fabricated parser for a private tag syntax. Invalid schemas are rejected rather than receiving an invented format reward. Empty-versus-empty edit similarity1, population standard deviation and delta1e-8 are declared boundary conventions. There is no language model, constrained decoder, label completion, SFT, GRPO parameter training, distillation or serving. References enter only the reward evaluator; no agent can read gold.
comparison.tradeoff: LARF models five ordinal relevance attributes of one document with PNR, rule feedback and terminal-digit margins. OneQuery instead supervises four heterogeneous structured fields of one query. Its QT reward requires whole-set exact matching, not LARF's graded distance or inter-document ordering. LARF's training generation/serving classification split also differs from OneQuery's head cache/tail distillation. Their production metrics are not directly comparable.

comparison.position: The component executes Equations5–7 and9–15 on supplied domain states/candidates: real two-layer PCNs, linear factor maps, one active-only MHA layer, domain gates/classifier, GRL, orthogonality and sampled softmax. Multi-modal encoders, RQ-VAE/semantic codebooks, item/history backbones, Equation8 task-level cold-start loss, complete LTN and the three-stage trainer are absent; this is not full CAMAR. Bias-free factor maps, MHA details and MLP hidden widths are declared local choices where the paper does not uniquely specify them.
comparison.tradeoff: LazUnirec uses private LoRA/experts and directional-reliability weights across retrieval/ranking tasks. CAMAR splits invariant/specific factors across song/playlist/podcast and permits only invariant cross-domain interaction. The former controls shared-update conflict; the latter constrains representation flow and domain distinguishability. Stable gradients do not establish domain invariance, and orthogonal inner products do not establish statistical independence. Neither private data nor local synthetic diagnostics support a direct quality ranking.
